newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-Coffee vols up as futures rebounds.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Coffee vols up as futures rebounds.

text.p: Coffee volatilities were chased higher on the LIFFE options pit on Wednesday as the futures market whip-sawed back up again after tumbling on Monday.
Cocoa options saw modest interest in out-of-the money calls but volume was razor-thin as the offers were few and far apart.
"There's still very good interest in out-of-the-money calls," said one market maker. "But unfortunately, no volume is being offered."
July vols saw bids at 28 percent and offers at 33-34 percent. The July vols were traded at 27 percent last week.
Market operators preferred to wait and see, watching the movements in the futures before committing themselves.
The interest in July calls centred on 1,050 and 1,100 strikes.
The futures market remained trapped in a range, with May being capped at near 1,035-1,037 stg resistance. A move higher would ensure a progress towards 1,100 stg.
By late Wednesday, May was traded 10 stg up at 1,026 after a high of 1,035.

In coffee options, the market saw locals marking up vols as the futures market were called $260 higher on paper on Wednesday after a fall by more than $100 since Monday. But it managed only $95 at the opening.
Activity gained some momentum today after a lull since Monday as operators stepped back amid falling futures values.
"They held back looking for clearer market signs," said one trader. "There were no new orders around."

Volume reached 641 lots on Wednesday and May vols were offered up to 47-48 percent against last week's 42 percent. July vols also remained firm as players took protection against the Brazilian frost risk.
The main interest on Wednesday centred on May $1,800 calls and July $1,100 and $1,200 puts.
